task: red-green contract quality gate — mutation testing as the fifth enforcement tooth, proving that every AC's verifier really bites the production code it claims to guard

items.scenario: Run the mutation check against an always-green verifier (the tautological kind); it must judge the target dead and end with a failing exit code
items.expect: rgm_mutation check prints DEAD and the process exits non-zero

items.scenario: Run the mutation check against a verifier that genuinely asserts the return value of the function under test; at least one mutation flips it from green to red, so the target is judged alive and it exits successfully
items.expect: rgm_mutation check prints ALIVE and the process exits zero

items.scenario: After a mutation check finishes normally, the mutated production file must be byte-for-byte identical to what it was before the run, leaving zero residue in the working tree
items.expect: Hashing the target file before and after the run yields exactly the same digest

items.scenario: When the verifier crashes or times out during mutation, the restore logic must still put the target file back, proving the finally-based restore works on the exception path
items.expect: After the verifier exits abnormally, the target file is still byte-for-byte identical to before the run

items.scenario: Run the mutation check against an acceptance item that declares no guarded targets; it must be judged not applicable and must not fail the gate
items.expect: rgm_mutation check prints N/A and the process exits zero

items.scenario: Feed a dead-target acceptance item into the aggregate gate with the mutation sub-check enabled; the whole gate must fail and the mutation sub-check must be marked failed
items.expect: With mutation enabled, rgm_gate's aggregate verdict is FAIL and the MUTATION sub-item is FAIL
